summary: When a worker registers activities with duplicate function names where one has an alias and one doesn't, invoking the non-aliased activity silently gets redirected to the aliased version. This occurs because the getActivityFunctionName function prioritizes alias lookups over the explicitly requested registration name.
userImpact: Users registering versioned activities with the same function name but different implementations experience silent routing to the wrong activity version, breaking workflow logic.
rootCause: The getActivityFunctionName function finds an alias registered for a given function name and resolves to that alias instead of respecting the explicitly registered name, causing unintended activity invocation.
proposedFix: Use fully qualified names in the registration map (e.g., map[activities_v1.Activity] instead of map[Activity]) to prevent collisions. Alternatively, default DisableRegistrationAliasing to true as a breaking change.
workaround: Set DisableRegistrationAliasing: true in worker options when using aliases, and avoid invoking activities using function pointers when aliases are in use.
keyQuote: The function getActivityFunctionName finds an alias registered for the given function name and resolves with the function attached to the alias
